title: Decode the Slanted Ciphertext
summary: Given an encoded string encodedText and the number of rows rows, decode the original string originalText using a slanted transposition cipher.
statement: Given an encoded string encodedText and the number of rows rows, decode the original string originalText using a slanted transposition cipher. The original text is placed in a matrix in a top-left to bottom-right manner, followed by filling the matrix by color order (blue, red, yellow), and then reading the matrix row-wise to form encodedText. The matrix columns are adjusted so that the rightmost column is not empty. The original text is returned without trailing spaces, and each test case has a unique solution.
constraints: encoded_text length is divisible by rows and represents the row-wise contents of the encoding matrix.
Read diagonals starting in the top row, moving down one row and right one column.
Remove trailing spaces only; preserve spaces inside the decoded message.
hints: The encoded string is a row-major matrix with len(text)//rows columns.
Start once at every top-row column and walk down-right until leaving the matrix.
Append matrix[row][start+row] for each valid row, then rstrip the result.
Those diagonals are exactly the original write order; right stripping removes only encoding padding.
editorial: Those diagonals are exactly the original write order; right stripping removes only encoding padding.
